title: IF I AM BEREAVED, I AM BEREAVED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then their father Israel said to them, 'If it must be, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your bags and take them down to the man as a gift—a little balm and a little honey, some spices and myrrh, some pistachio nuts and almonds. Take double the amount of silver with you, for you must return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake. Take your brother also and go back to the man at once. And may God Almighty grant you mercy before the man so that he will let your other brother and Benjamin come back with you. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.'" - Gen 43:11-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last, Jacob surrenders. He sends gifts of the land's best, double the silver to return what was found in their sacks, and — most costly of all — Benjamin. And he releases the outcome to God with a prayer and a sigh of faith: "May God Almighty grant you mercy... As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved."

What a change from his earlier despair, "Everything is against me!" (Gen 42:36). Now Jacob calls on "God Almighty" — El Shaddai, the God of his fathers — and entrusts the situation to Him. He has moved from clutching in fear to opening his hands in faith. He still does not know how it will end, but he places it in God's hands.

That final phrase — "if I am bereaved, I am bereaved" — is the language of surrender. It is not fatalism or despair, but a trusting release: "I have done what I can; now the outcome rests with God, and I accept whatever He allows." It echoes Esther's brave words, "If I perish, I perish" (Esth 4:16), and even our Lord's, "Not my will, but yours be done" (Luke 22:42).

There comes a point in every trial where we must open our clenched hands and entrust the outcome to God. We do what wisdom requires, we pray for His mercy, and then we release the result to Him. That surrender is not weakness; it is faith. What are you still clutching that God is asking you to release into His hands?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I moved from clutching in fear to opening my hands in faith?
2. Can I entrust the outcome of my trial to God and accept His will?
3. What do I need to release, saying, "Lord, Your will be done"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: God Almighty, I bring my situation to You and ask for Your mercy. Help me to open my clenched hands and entrust the outcome to You. Whatever You allow, I say, "Your will be done." Amen.
